I read it twice. The line that stopped me was the one about income, gains and friends reading badly, and about spending and time away from home. That is my life since 2008 set down in a sentence: no gains, no friends left, and a room I do not leave. Whoever wrote it did not know who I was, or it would have been written differently, and that is why I take those two lines seriously.

The rest I am less sure about. It says money and family life read well, and work and standing read well. For most of my life a stranger looking at me would have said exactly that, so the reading was right for forty-eight years and catastrophically wrong for the last one. Maybe that is the honest limit of the thing. It does not tell you which way a man will turn.

It says I am steady and self-reliant and happier leading than following. That is true, and it is also true of every man I ever sat across a table from. It flatters. I know something about how a person is flattered into believing a page in front of them.

On my father it is generous, and I let it be generous. He lost what he had and I watched it, and I do not think I ever stopped answering to that. On higher study it is simply wrong. I got a degree, I quit law school after a year, and nothing I did afterward came out of a classroom.

What it does not have, and cannot have, is the only question worth asking about me. My sons are not in it.
